title: fix(service-knowledge): record-change sync honours the source where; a restored record re-enters the index
body:
Fixes #36991

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读
- 用户能看到什么变化：挂了知识检索的应用里，知识源只索引符合条件的记录（例如只索引现行版本）；记录改成不符合后，旧内容从检索结果里消失；从回收站恢复的记录，符合条件就能重新被搜到。
- 为什么做：知识检索平台化专题第一阶段的「结果要对」——此前记录变更时完全不看索引条件，草稿会进索引，失效内容一直搜得到。
- 出错会怎样：只影响挂了知识检索服务的应用的检索结果，保存记录本身不受影响；改动可直接撤回，撤回后回到旧行为。
- 要你做的：无。

## What changes

`KnowledgeService.handleRecordUpsert` no longer builds the document from the event payload. With a data engine bound, each `object` source bound to the object re-reads the row under the system context, `find(object, { where: { $and: [where, { id }] }, limit: 1 }, { context: system })` (`{ id }` alone when the source has no `where`):

- a row comes back: the document is built from the re-read row through the same `recordToDocument(source, objSource, row, this.schemaFor(object))` gate as the reindex walk, so the credential-class / `internal` withholding landed by #36850 holds on this path too, and the document carries the fields the source lists and the record `title`, never a credential-class or `internal` field;
- no row: the document is deleted (idempotent).

The plugin's event bridge now routes `data.record.restored` (`RECORD_RESTORED_EVENT` from `@objectstack/spec/data`) through the same path; its comment and the `enableEventSync` option docs name all four per-record events. With no data engine: a source without `where` still builds from the payload; a source with `where` is skipped and reported once per source at `warn`. Syncs of one document (`${source.id}:${recordId}`, upserts and deletes alike) run through an in-process promise chain, dropped when idle, so two opposite events cannot interleave. The system context is one helper now shared with `reindexSource` (same spelling it already used). No adapter-contract member, no spec change, no queue.

`content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx` section 6 is rewritten to say this, including the measured ordering below; it also drops the claim that a bare `record.*` event is still accepted (the bridge has had no branch for it).

### Item 6: where the event fires relative to the write's transaction (measured on origin/main 8aecf6d7)

- `data.record.created` is published at `packages/objectql/src/engine-insert.ts:1716`, inside the engine body that `insert` wraps in its own unit when it opens one (`engine-insert.ts:386`, `executeWithMiddleware(opCtx, inOwnUnit(...))`, closing at :1805); `data.record.updated` at `engine-update.ts:2445`, inside `inOwnUnit` opened at `engine-update.ts:529`. So both fire before that unit, or a caller's `engine.transaction(...)`, commits.
- `publishDataEvent` awaits `realtimeService.publish` (`engine-realtime-publish.ts:484`), and the in-process adapter awaits each subscriber (`packages/services/service-realtime/src/in-memory-realtime-adapter.ts:98`), so the knowledge handler runs inside the write's async context. A read with no explicit transaction takes the ambient one (`engine-driver-options.ts:304-306`), so the re-read sees the row the write just made. A rolled-back unit leaves the index wrong until the row's next event or a `reindexSource`, in one of two ways: if the uncommitted row matched, the document stays built from a row that never committed (as the payload path did); if it did not match, the document was deleted, so the committed row, which may still match, is missing from the index (new with the re-read). Because the sync is inline, a write's sync can also wait behind an earlier in-flight sync of the same document (on a single-connection pool, up to the acquire timeout); the index still ends consistent.
- `data.record.restored` is published at `recycle-bin/restore.ts:470`, after `writeBack` (:451) has run and committed the restore's own unit (`restore.ts:756`).
- Bulk `data.records.*` events stay uncovered; the existing warn and doc callout say so.

## Tests

`src/__tests__/event-sync-data-events.test.ts` is rewritten (it asserted building from `after`): the bridge cases now cover `data.record.restored`, and the sync cases run the real plugin and service against an engine double whose `find` applies scalar equality and `$and`, refuses any other operator by throwing, and applies `limit` by presence after the filter. One test per acceptance item: enter on match; does not enter when not matching; exit when a record stops matching (and search no longer finds it); no `where`; payload missing a content field; restored and matching is searchable; restored but not matching is not indexed; no engine without `where`; no engine with `where` (skipped, one warn across two events); and three two-event races (match then no match, no match then match, update then delete) each ending consistent with the database. In `knowledge-service.test.ts` the event-path withholding pin now feeds a payload carrying only the id and a re-read row carrying the credential and internal fields, under `'*'` and named explicitly.

Ablations, each through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor hit 1 to 0, blob changed, restored to HEAD with `git diff HEAD` empty); the test imports the source by relative path, so no `dist/` leg:

| Mutation | Red |
|---|---|
| re-read `where` reduced to `{ id }` | 5 of 23 (query shape, not matching, stops matching, restored not matching, match-then-no-match race) |
| serialization removed from the upsert path | 3 of 23 (all three races) |
| `RECORD_RESTORED_EVENT` dropped from the bridge | 2 of 23 (restored routing, restored searchable); a first attempt with the anchor ending in a bare close-paren-brace was refused by the tool before any run (replacement count did not move), and was re-run with a unique anchor |
| document built from the payload instead of the re-read row | 3 of 51 across both files (both withholding pins, missing-content-field) |

## Acceptance notes

- Under `contentFields: ['*']` the event-path document now carries every string field of the re-read row, exactly what `reindexSource` already sends for the same row; explicit lists send only the listed fields. Retiring `'*'` is the epic's row 3, not this card.
- The per-document chain orders syncs in one process only; two processes publishing for one row are not ordered by it (the card scopes item 5 to in-process).
- The sync stays inline with the write (as before): a write now also waits for one system-context read per bound source.

## Verification

Two minutes: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-knowledge exec vitest run src/__tests__/event-sync-data-events.test.ts` should print `Tests  23 passed (23)`.

2. `packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-service-plugin.ts`: the event-bridge branch now including `RECORD_RESTORED_EVENT`.
3. `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx` section 6: the ordering statement.
